correctness.rationale: In any forest with m marked vertices, a singleton component contributes no nonsingleton marked-vertex trace and a size-two component duplicates one. With a,b,c marked components of sizes 1,2,>=3, and h outside vertices meeting >=2 marked components, acyclicity of their contracted incidence forest gives h<=a+b+c-1, hence |T|<=m+1+(m-a-b)+h<=2m+c<=2m+floor(m/3). For m=3q equality forces q marked P3 components, h=q-1 outside 2-neighbour vertices whose incidence subdivision contracts to a block tree, and all singleton/empty traces. The converse tree construction has 3q marked points, 3q private leaves, q-1 connectors and one empty-trace vertex, total 7q. Triple and pair traces uniquely decode partitions, centres, tree edges and attachment choices, so the exact formula follows by three-block partitions times 3^q centres times Cayley q^(q-2) times 9^(q-1). Replayed exhaustive checks on <=6 vertices and q=1,2 are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The natural graph-neighbourhood type invariant already has a sharp 7/3 numerical bound, but that does not answer which complete parameter-labelled Boolean trace systems realize saturation. The theorem provides the complete rigidity normal form, a 3q-block combinatorial structure, exact all-q number (first values 3,810,1837080) and minimum realization order 7q. This is a non-arbitrary zero-slack extremal classification linked directly to the motivating sharp theorem; no external downstream theorem is required. It does not republish the prior numerical bound as its own claim.
